item.text:
**Bottom Line**
No. In 2024 Hasina did not strengthen independent courts, legislature, anti-corruption bodies, local governments, or oversight institutions. The record instead shows politicized courts and anti-corruption enforcement, a parliament too weak to scrutinize the executive, and an election commission seen as non-independent. The only narrow counterevidence is that the Supreme Court briefly constrained the quota policy in July 2024, but that was reactive and does not show institutional strengthening by Hasina.

- [Bangladesh: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-world/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Claim: the Awami League consolidated power through harassment of the opposition and critical media; anticorruption efforts were weakened by politicized enforcement; the dearth of opposition representation significantly reduced Parliament’s ability to scrutinize policy and budgets; and the Election Commission’s independence was widely questioned. This is direct evidence against strengthening independent oversight institutions. `4B.4`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Bangladesh: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/bangladesh/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Claim: the government maintained criminal speech controls and a partisan information environment; the judicial system was formally independent but critics said the Ministry of Law played a politicized role in assigning, removing, and transferring judges. This is direct evidence against strengthening independent courts and oversight. `4B.4`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `3B.8`

- [Bangladesh: Repression, Security Force Abuses Discredit Elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024. Claim: authorities suppressed dissent, arrested people for criticism, and undermined the pledge of a free and fair vote through widespread repression and violence. That is inconsistent with building independent institutions that can constrain the executive. `4B.4`, `4B.1`, `4B.3`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Bangladesh turnout low in election set to keep PM Hasina in power](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-turnout-low-in-election-set-to-keep-pm-hasina-in-power-3268699) — Reuters, January 7, 2024. Claim: the main opposition boycotted the election and Reuters described the contest as one set to keep Hasina in power rather than a genuinely competitive process. This supports the view that the legislature and electoral system were not being strengthened as independent checks. `4B.4`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`

- [Little election fizz in Bangladesh as prime minister set for another term](https://theprint.in/world/little-election-fizz-in-bangladesh-as-prime-minister-set-for-another-term/1910693/) — Reuters, January 4, 2024. Claim: the opposition boycott followed Hasina’s refusal to resign and allow a neutral authority to run the election. This is direct evidence against empowering independent election oversight or neutral institutions. `4B.4`, `4B.1`, `4B.2`

- [Bangladesh court scraps most job quotas that sparked deadly protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-extends-curfew-ahead-of-court-hearing-on-controversial-job-quotas-3527975) — Reuters, July 21, 2024. Claim: the Supreme Court scrapped most government-job quotas after the student protests had escalated. This is the closest counterevidence on institutional constraint, but it is a court reacting under crisis, not evidence that Hasina strengthened judicial independence in 2024. `4B.4`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`

- [Bangladesh’s crackdown left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — UN/OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Claim: the UN said more than 170 people were killed and warned that internet shutdowns increased impunity. This reinforces that oversight and accountability institutions were not being strengthened in practice. `4B.4`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `4B.1`

**Search gap**
I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Hasina strengthened local government autonomy, audit bodies, or parliamentary scrutiny. The strongest available material points the other way: politicized courts, weakened anticorruption enforcement, and a parliament/election commission that did not operate as an independent check.
